title: For a Cartesian square Y→T over X→S, a closed immersion i:Z→T, and the corresponding Cartesian square YZ→Z, the canonical target transition is an isomorphism with coefficient i_*G.
statement: Let Λ be a commutative ring and q an integer. Let e:Y→T, h:Y→X, g:T→S, p:X→S form a Cartesian square. Let i:Z→T be a closed immersion and let eZ:YZ→Z and hZ:YZ→X form a Cartesian square over i≫g and p. Let a:YZ→Y satisfy a≫e=eZ≫i and a≫h=hZ. For every sheaf G of Λ-modules on Z, the canonical target transition of [def-sbc-module-higher-image-transitions], from the target for e,h with coefficient i_*G to the target for eZ,hZ with coefficient i^*i_*G, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0F07, closed coefficient comparison, using 03QP and 0959

proof.text: Paste the two given pullback squares to obtain a pullback square eZ,a,i,e. The base change a of i is closed. Finite base change [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] identifies e^*i_*G with a_*eZ^*G.

For a closed immersion i, finite direct image is exact [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] and closed pushforward is fully faithful [prop-openclosed-lowerstar-fully-faithful]. The Lean proof uses the already-proved cover-dense and locally full/faithful refinement of this latter statement, in Etale.UpperLowerStar.ClosedImmersion, with module coefficients.

The ordinary counit is invertible. On a complex, its componentwise image and its homotopy-category image are invertible. The derived counit factorization and the invertible exact-functor derived unit then imply the bounded-below derived counit is invertible. Consequently the derived right adjoint is fully faithful. The single complex of i_*G is isomorphic, by exactness and the single-functor comparison, to Ri_* applied to G[0]. The derived adjunction unit is therefore invertible there.

The exact inverse-image single-functor comparison and finite base-change isomorphism identify D(e^*) applied to (i_*G)[0] with (a_*eZ^*G)[0]. Transport invertibility of the derived unit for a across this isomorphism. As in the source argument, derived-unit composition coherence expresses the lower-star transition as the image of this unit followed by an invertible derived direct-image composition comparison. Every remaining factor of the target transition is an inverse-image composition comparison, equality transport or single-functor comparison, hence invertible. Apply homology.

theorem baseChangeTargetTransition_isIso_closed_coefficients
    {X S T Y Z YZ : Scheme.{u}} {p : X ⟶ S} {g : T ⟶ S}
    {e : Y ⟶ T} {h : Y ⟶ X} (sq : IsPullback e h g p)
    (i : Z ⟶ T) [IsClosedImmersion i] {eZ : YZ ⟶ Z} {hZ : YZ ⟶ X}
    (sqZ : IsPullback eZ hZ (i ≫ g) p) (a : YZ ⟶ Y)
    (wa : a ≫ e = eZ ≫ i) (wh : a ≫ h = hZ) (q : ℤ)
    (G : Sheaf Z.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) :
    IsIso (baseChangeTargetTransition Λ e h q i a eZ hZ wa wh
      (((i)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ]).obj G))
